Nature & food

bean noun

also beans

classical

Verg. G. I 227: vīlemque phasēlum
Columella X 377

phasēlus, phasēlī m.

noun, second declension

the pod bean

The modern green and kidney beans are an American species that inherited the ancient name (Phaseolus vulgaris, Linn.); Ep. VII uses phasēlī of Baba’s garden. The bean words divide cleanly: faba is the ancient broad bean, phasēlus the pod bean whose name the American Phaseolus inherited, pīsum the pea.

Examples

  • Jūs ē phasēlīs coquitur.

    Bean soup is cooking.composed

See also broad bean, pea, pulses.

SourcesLewis & Short: phaselus

Theodōrus et pater: Ep. III (cicer in the cēna rūstica, with the gloss legūmen rotundum), Ep. IV (lēns, faba, cicer in the cella penāria), Ep. VII (phasēlī in Baba’s garden).
